To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
there is enough information to move forward with EBSAs and marine spatial planning for conservation purposes, and that the time is right for this to happen.

(i) there is enough information about marine ecosystems of the Mediterranean to move forward with conservation planning; (ii) there is a political will to do so; (iii) the Mediterranean Sea is an excellent case study of how to advance conservation in a complex and highly diverse region; and (iv) the proposed model process can be used to achieve conservation targets in the Mediterranean Sea and elsewhere.

Although significant advancements on protecting the marine biodiversity and ecosystems in the Mediterranean have been made, there is still a long way to go to achieve the 2020 target of 10% marine protected area coverage and the process to get there is not straightforward.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following questions: What are the current and potential conservation planning efforts in the Mediterranean Sea and what is their status?
how to best use the information we have to move towards a more sustainable use of the Mediterranean Sea, and to do so now.
the need to develop a conservation strategy for the Mediterranean that will be implemented by the Mediterranean governments.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the Mediterranean Sea is a unique and complex region, and the process of marine spatial planning and conservation is a complex one that requires a multi-stakeholder, multi-scale, and multi-disciplinary approach to achieve its goals.

the Mediterranean Sea is in a state of ecological crisis, that the Mediterranean Sea faces a number of serious threats, and that the time is ripe for a new and comprehensive conservation approach to be implemented.
the Mediterranean is ready for a major leap forward on conservation and that the time is now.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the Mediterranean Sea is a complex region with a rich history of conservation initiatives and that the current political context offers an unprecedented opportunity to make significant progress towards achieving the CBD targets.
we need to act now to protect the Mediterranean Sea.

1) the Mediterranean is a complex region with many stakeholders and a history of conflict; 2) there is sufficient information available to start planning and designing an ecologically representative marine protected area network for the Mediterranean Sea; and 3) the time is now to start the process of planning and designing an ecosystem-based network of marine protected area for the Mediterranean Sea.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Mediterranean region has the potential for a major breakthrough in marine conservation if the process we outline is followed.
we can no longer wait for the perfect data set or the best conservation planning tool to advance the cause of marine conservation in the Mediterranean.
the Mediterranean is not a lost cause, and that there is a window of opportunity to advance conservation in this highly complex and politically charged environment.
